channel.title: Joseph Bankole's blog
channel.description: Field notes by Joseph Bankole on payment infrastructure, ISO 20022 migrations and running AI agents in production, written up from the work itself.

item.title: The BS Guide
item.description: A practical guide to setting Claude up to handle the boring parts of your job: a project, a handover document, the first five tasks to delegate, connected tools, and the rules that keep you out of trouble.

item.title: A search summary is not a source
item.description: A web search summary dropped three names from a seventeen-member list, invented a table, and returned a URL that was a 404. What I fetch before I cite.

item.title: The IntersectionObserver threshold my content outgrew
item.description: A homepage block rendered as 6,164 pixels of empty background. The IntersectionObserver threshold never changed; the list under it grew one row a day.

item.title: Per-item checks cannot see the batch
item.description: Nine pieces of copy passed nine rotation checks on the same morning, and six of the nine ended the same way. Why item-scoped validation misses a collapsing distribution.

item.title: Automated audits fail toward false positives
item.description: Five checks in my own site audit failed in five runs. Every one was confidently wrong, and every one invented work. The tells that catch them, and the fixes.

item.title: The carousel that rendered blank
item.description: A renderer started shipping carousels where the first card was blank. Blank-on-the-first-one is a tell. It almost always means a race.

item.title: The production AI bug that was the context window
item.description: Two AI agents started failing the same way. The root cause was context-window exhaustion as a production failure mode, and the fixes were classic operations, not AI magic.

item.title: The architecture of a multi-agent content operation
item.description: A content operation that is almost entirely automated: scheduled agents that generate, queue, measure, and adjust. The models write fine. The hard part is everything around the model.

item.title: What actually happens when a payment batch fails
item.description: A failed batch is not one problem. It is thousands of payments sharing one problem. The triage order matters more than speed.

item.title: What an ISO 20022 migration actually breaks first
item.description: ISO 20022 is not a date on a calendar. From inside payment operations it is a long list of small things that break quietly. Here is what goes first.
